claims.claim: Reviewers describe the narrative and commentary provided by the voice actor as a standout, humorous aspect of the game.

citations.review_text:
The Stanley Parable is proof that you can make an entire game out of walking through an office and ignoring instructions.

The narrator is absolutely fantastic. Every time you make a choice — especially when you deliberately do the opposite of what you're told — the game reacts in hilarious and increasingly ridiculous ways.

The writing is clever, self-aware, and constantly messing with your expectations. It doesn't just give you choices; it makes you question why you even want to make them in the first place.

There isn't much traditional gameplay, but that's completely intentional. The fun comes from experimenting, finding different endings, and seeing how far you can push the game's logic.

It's short, hilarious, weirdly philosophical, and somehow manages to stay memorable long after you've finished it.

**10/10 — the narrator told me exactly what to do. Naturally, I did the opposite.**
Its a maze through offices with many many... many halls trying to find the ending, which there are a lot of. Game itself isn't spectacular but the voice over makes it so entertaining!

claims.claim: Reviewers mention receiving an achievement for not playing the game for five years.

citations.review_text: The only reason I stopped playing for 5 years was to get the achievement. Game is highly enjoyable

Just got the "Go outside" achievement when I realized I haven't played The Stanley Parable in 5 years, from then till now, I moved to Toronto, got my own car, got my first tattoo, lost weight and got in shape, it's so surreal to get that achievement when 5 years ago I was wishing I hadn't played The Stanley Parable for 5 years to get the achievement then. What a fun story.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Players note the simple walking simulator mechanics paired with a narrator reacting to disobedience.

claims.claim: This cohort describes the gameplay as a walking simulator where mechanics are limited to moving, crouching, and pressing buttons.

citations.review_text:
The Stanley Parable is an incredible experience. A game commenting on games themselves, their characters, and plot structures. Just be aware this is more walking simulator with some interactive elements, however each playthrough is very quick. If this is your first time playing this, you are in for a treat. 

You play as the titular Stanley, and you have to make choices. Very specific choices. Very important choices. Or none at all. That, too, is a choice.

Kevan Brighting as the Narrator is simply sublime. Funny, emotional, and utterly British. He reacts to your choices. He hates your choices. He praises your choices. He questions your choices. 

Do you have any choices? Are you Stanley? Am I Stanley? There's only one way to find out - play The Stanley Parable today!

Rating = 9 out of 10

[h1][b]About[/b][/h1]
You are Stanley. One day you stop receiving orders and "wake up".
[hr][/hr]
[h1][b]Gameplay[/b][/h1]
The Stanley Parable a Walking Simulator in it's purest form. You can crouch and press buttons but that's your lot. 

[h1][b]Design[/b][/h1]
Using Half-life 2's Source Engine, the graphics a basic and levels simple. But what makes this game a crown jewel amongst the myriad of walking simulators is the writing and narration. From simple commentary, witty jokes to thought provoking monologues, the narrator is the true character of this game.


[h1][b]Verdict[/b] [i]★★★★★[/i][/h1]
You can finish this game in an hour, or two if you really experiment. This is the original 2013 release of the game which is still a fantastic game but if you can, I'd recommend picking up the ultra deluxe version of the game, it's got everything in this release plus MORE!

One of the pioneering games of walking simulators and a must play for anyone looking for an interactive audiobook.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the voice acting and narration as a standout element that reacts dynamically to player choices.

citations.review_text:
[h2]Am I Stanley? Stanley is mean to me.[/h2]

Stanley is everything, and everything is Stanley. At least that’s the general idea behind this bizarre psychological social experiment that someone somehow turned into a video game.

The strange thing is… it’s actually really good.

The graphics are decent enough, but the real highlight is the narration and the way the game constantly reacts to your choices. The flow of events can either delight you or completely drive you insane depending on how stubborn you decide to be. One moment you’ll be laughing, and the next you’ll be arguing with a narrator who clearly enjoys tormenting you.

Overall, it’s an incredibly unique experience and absolutely worth playing at least once. If only Stanley would finally make a sequel already. Oh wait… there kind of is one.

Just remember: without Stanley, there would be no game. That includes you reading this, Stanley.

[h2]8/10[/h2]

claims.claim: This cohort mentions specific achievements that require leaving the game running for an entire twenty-four-hour Tuesday or abstaining from playing for five years.

citations.review_text:
I really don't know what compelled me to 100% this game. I did all the achievements legitimately besides "Go Outside" (I am NOT waiting 5 years)
Yes, that means I played this for an entire Tuesday

The only reason I have so many hours here, is one particular achievement that literally requires you to leave your computer on an entire specific day. I messed up once and had to do it again.

That said achievements are a separate thing, theres maybe only three you wouldn't get with a normal game experience.

That experience is fun. This game is not challenging, and by nature a little repetitive- that said, my first ending was "confusion" and it really delivered. Lots of endings to discover, and the narrator is a pleasure to listen to.
